subject: Cloud Computing
title: Government Moves to the Cloud
description: A micro-lesson that makes Government Moves to the Cloud usable.

hook.text: In 2011, the U.S. announced 'Cloud First' — a mandate to move government agencies to the cloud.

buildup.text: Government data centers were aging, expensive, and often running at just 27% capacity.

discovery.text: The CIA signed a $600 million deal with AWS, proving the cloud could meet top-secret needs.

twist.text: IBM sued over the contract and lost. It marked the moment cloud officially beat traditional IT.

climax.text: Today, every major government relies on cloud services. Even spy agencies trust them.

punchline.text: If the CIA trusts the cloud, your startup probably can too.

quiz.question: What did the CIA's $600 million AWS contract prove?
options: Cloud computing could meet even top-secret security requirements
The government planned to replace all spies with cloud AI
AWS was the cheapest option for basic file storage

details.summary: Governments worldwide have adopted cloud computing to modernize aging IT systems, reduce costs, and improve citizen services. The US FedRAMP program and equivalent frameworks in other countries created compliance standards that enabled cloud adoption in the public sector.
details.whyItMatters: Government cloud adoption validates cloud security and reliability at the highest trust levels. Compliance frameworks developed for government use benefit the entire industry.
takeaways: FedRAMP provides compliance standards for government cloud use
Governments save billions by migrating from legacy systems
Government-grade security frameworks benefit all cloud customers

faq.question: What is FedRAMP in practice?
faq.answer: The Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program is a US government compliance framework for cloud services. It provides standardized security assessment and authorization for cloud products used by federal agencies, ensuring they meet strict security and privacy requirements.

faq.question: Do cloud providers have special government regions?
faq.answer: Yes. AWS GovCloud, Azure Government, and Google Cloud for Government offer dedicated regions meeting government compliance requirements. These regions are physically separated, operated by screened personnel, and meet specific regulatory standards like FedRAMP High and ITAR.
